statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-3833 (GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-5): GnuTLS before 3.8.13 compares domain names case-sensitively when it applies name constraints, contrary to RFC 5280 section 7.2, so a name that an excluded constraint should reject can be accepted. GnuTLS fixes it in 3.8.13 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html), and Alpine lists it as fixed in gnutls 3.8.13-r0 for 3.23 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-3833). This owner is built from Alpine's gnutls package source for 3.23. Its published gnutls packages for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64, are 3.8.11-r0 and 3.8.12-r0, whose libgnutls library reports GnuTLS 3.8.11 and 3.8.12, and the current 3.8.13-r0, whose library reports GnuTLS 3.8.13. The range ends at 3.8.13-r0.

CVE-2026-3833: GnuTLS compared dNSName and rfc822Name name-constraint labels case-sensitively, so a leaf certificate whose Subject Alternative Name differs only in letter case could bypass permitted or excluded subtrees and be accepted. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-5 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-5, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1803) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/19f6508647bdcd3ce21130201e484d7ca6d962c5 ("x509/name-constraints: compare domain names case-insensitive"). Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-3833), which applies the GnuTLS 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9 and carries that upstream commit. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version, and the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 lists CVE-2026-3833 under 3.8.9-3+deb13u4. The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources predate the fix and sort below it, so they are reported as affected.
